prompt: What is $10^5$ written as a regular number?
hint: The small raised number is an exponent. It tells how many tens are multiplied together.

hints.text: The small raised number is an exponent. It tells how many tens are multiplied together.
Write out five tens: $10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10$. Each multiplication by ten puts one more zero after the $1$.
Five tens multiplied together make a $1$ with five zeros, so $10^5 = 100{,}000$.

explanation: The exponent $5$ means five factors of $10$: $10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10$.
Each $\times 10$ tacks on one zero, starting from $1$.
Five zeros gives $100{,}000$, which we read as one hundred thousand.

alternativeExplanations.title: Build it up
steps: Each step multiplies by $10$ again: $10^4 = 10{,}000$ and $10^5 = 100{,}000$ ✓
